paper_metadata.title: Effect of two-phase microstructure characteristics on high strain rate elastoplastic deformation of superalloys: A three-dimensional discrete dislocation dynamics study

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: The two-phase microstructure may bring excellent mechanical properties to materials such as superalloys used for advanced turbine engines.
the present work studies the strain rate (2 × 10 3 s 1) in-between
it might be more physical to have dislocation glide only in the present case of single crystal Ni-based superalloys.

samples.original_name: Ni-based single crystal superalloy with γ matrix channel width 60 nm

evidence.section: 3.1 Effect of matrix channel width on elastoplastic deformation
evidence.quote: By setting three different γ matrix channel widths (60 nm,80 nm and 100 nm), the effect of γ matrix channel width on elastoplastic deformation is studied. The APB energy, γ’ precipitate volume fraction and γ/γ’ misfit are fixed to 125 mJ/m2, 67.5 % and 0.003, respectively.

evidence.section: 2.1 Simulation setup
evidence.quote: When a dislocation segment cuts into the γ’ precipitate, the resulting sheared area transforms into an anti-phase boundary (APB), possessing a free energy that exceeds twice the energy of the γ/γ’ interface.
Dislocations multiply in the γ matrix channels at the early stage of plastic deformation and pile up at γ / γ’ interfaces due to the resistance of γ’ APB energy.
it is always beneficial to have bigger APB energy by adding some rare earth elements. It is also beneficial to increase the volume fraction of γ’ precipitates up to a critical point
the strong hardening of higher γ’ precipitate volume fraction is not from the line tension resistance caused by the curvature of dislocation.
